claims: Agencies charge ~$30,000/year for an 'AI inbound autopilot' that tracks visitors and emails them; you can build it yourself with Jev + PostHog
Wait about two weeks after installing PostHog to have enough visitor data
Identification tools only find a visitor's email ~20% of the time if they have not opted in
Jev response on screen: persona 'investor' with confidence 0.94 (decision_maker 0.04, job_applicant 0.01, junior_champion 0.02)
PostHog dashboard sample: 878 visitors, 1.28K page views, 940 sessions, 2m 11s session duration
how_to_steps: Prompt 1: have your AI install PostHog on your existing landing page

Prompt 2: analyze PostHog data (where people click, what companies they are from) and cluster into visitor archetypes (e.g. Decision Maker, Investor, Job Applicant, Junior Champion, Veteran Sales Guy, Happy Customer, Competitor, Researcher)
Write one follow-up email per archetype
Prompt 3: build the system -- on $pageleave, check CRM (HubSpot) whether the person was already emailed; if not, send activity + IP data to Jev to predict archetype; send the matching email
If the visitor has not opted in, optionally use an identification tool (RB2B, Vector, Snitcher, Dealfront) to find their email (~20% hit rate)

relevance.why: A real growth mechanic for a B2B landing page, buildable with Claude Code in a day. But it depends on Jev (unverified) and de-anonymization vendors with privacy/legal exposure (GDPR/CCPA), and for consumer apps the archetype email play is weak.

implement_score.why: Simplified version is worth doing: PostHog on every landing page now (free tier), then after 2 weeks have Claude cluster visitors and tailor onboarding emails to opted-in signups. Skip IP de-anonymization and replace Jev with a cheap Claude/Haiku classification call. One day of work.

verify: Does TypeSafe's Jev / api.typesafe.ai exist, what does it cost, and is it better than a Haiku structured-output call for 4-way classification?
Legal: emailing people identified from IP/visitor-ID tools without opt-in (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CCPA); the 20% match claim
